title: Effect of Autologous Platelet-Rich Plasma with Autologous thrombin Serum in a Refractory Non-Healing Below-Knee Amputation Stump Wound: A Case Report
content: Introduction: Postoperative wound complications following below-knee amputation (BKA) require meticulous stump management to promote wound healing, control edema, and facilitate timely prosthetic fitting. Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) offers a regenerative, autologous option rich in growth factors to facilitate tissue repair. This case report describes the use of adjunctive PRP therapy in a refractory BKA stump wound that failed conventional wound management and repeated surgical interventions. Case Presentation: A 33-year-old male with a longstanding history of recurrent bilateral lower-extremity ulcerations, chronic osteomyelitis, and Charcot arthropathy presented with a persistent non-healing wound over his right BKA stump following amputation in September 2024. Despite multiple surgical debridement, wound excision, and primary closure attempts, a central dehiscence measuring 1.5 × 3.5 × 2.7 cm (14.18 cm³) persisted. Autologous PRP was applied directly to the wound bed at weekly intervals alongside compressive dressings. Outcomes: Serial wound assessments over four weeks demonstrated progressive wound bed regeneration, with complete granulation tissue formation, resolution of local edema, and a marked reduction in wound volume from 14.2 cm³ to 0.48 cm³ (approximately 97%). Complete epithelialization and wound closure were achieved without the need for further surgical intervention, enabling progression to prosthetic rehabilitation. Conclusion: This case suggests that adjunctive autologous PRP may be a useful regenerative option for promoting healing in selected patients with refractory below-knee amputation stump wounds when conventional management has failed. Further studies are warranted to establish its efficacy and optimal treatment protocol.
